title: SQL Injection authentication bypass
impact: An attacker can exploit the login form by inserting malicious SQL commands into the email field
remediation: potentially bypassing authentication and gaining unauthorized access to the administrator account and its restricted features
screenshot: Use prepared statements and parameterized queries to prevent malicious input from modifying SQL commands. Implement proper server-side authentication checks and limit repeated login attempts to reduce unauthorized access

title: UNION-based SQL Injection in product search
impact: An attacker can manipulate the product search query using a UNION SELECT statement to retrieve sensitive information from other database tables
remediation: including user email addresses and password hashes. This may lead to account compromise and unauthorized access to user information
screenshot: Replace dynamically constructed SQL queries with parameterized queries. Validate search inputs
column13: and avoid displaying detailed SQL error messages that could reveal information about the database structure

title: XSS via reflectd search input
impact: An attacker can insert malicious JavaScript into a specially crafted search URL
remediation: causing the script to execute when another user opens the link. This may allow unauthorized actions within the victim’s session or exposure of sensitive browser information
screenshot: Apply proper input validation and output encoding before displaying search parameters. Remove unsafe HTML-rendering functions and implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict the execution of malicious scripts

title: Stored XSS in customer feedback
impact: An attacker can submit feedback containing malicious JavaScript that remains stored in the application. The script may execute whenever an administrator views the affected feedback
remediation: potentially exposing administrator sessions or allowing unauthorized actions
screenshot: Sanitize user-submitted feedback before storing or displaying it. Avoid unsafe HTML rendering and implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) to prevent malicious scripts from executing in the administrator’s browser
